newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical industry confident for second half.
newsitem.headline: German chemical industry confident for second half.

text.p: The German chemical industry said that it was confident for the second half of 1996, despite the still unsatisfactory situation in the chemical industry.

Juergen Strube, head of the Association of German Chemical Companies (VCI) and also management board chairman at BASF AG, said "the companies expect more lively domestic demand in the second half, as well as ongoing strong sales abroad."
In the first half, Strube said, data for the chemical industry showed that the strong international orientation was "the right way".
Strube said chemical sales in the first half were around 89 billion marks, about 5.5 percent below the first half of 1995.
Exports totalled 52 billion marks rising one percent from year ago levels. The export quota rose to 58 percent.
Meanwhile imports dropped by two percent to around 31 billion marks. Due to the reduced domestic sales the import quota, however, rose to 45 percent.
Strube said that domestic demand, compared with a strong first half 1995, was "weak and clearly below year-ago levels".

Consequently production dropped by around 3.5 percent, with inorganic basic chemicals and plastics taking the biggest hit. On the other hand, production in agricultural chemicals and pharmaceuticals continued to grow.
